subject.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)

question: Should every operator-triggered cron run record its outcome while leaving deletion, counters, alerts, backoff, enabled state, and `nextRunAtMs` entirely owned by timer and Gateway watcher executions?
rationale: Preventing destructive manual deletion is clearly warranted, but making all operator outcomes non-consuming is a broader scheduler policy choice that changes existing counter, alert, retry, and timing behavior.

options.title: Confirm full operator isolation
options.body: Keep operator runs observational, but move watcher/timer origin selection behind an internal service boundary and require live upgrade/runtime proof.

options.title: Narrow the fix to deletion
options.body: Prevent manual `deleteAfterRun` consumption while retaining existing counter, alert, backoff, and scheduling behavior until those semantics are separately approved.

options.title: Retain the public origin option
options.body: Accept caller-selectable origins as supported API and document and compatibility-test which trusted consumers may request consuming scheduler behavior.

recommendation.title: Confirm full operator isolation
recommendation.body: Keep operator runs observational, but move watcher/timer origin selection behind an internal service boundary and require live upgrade/runtime proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cron runtime work and proximity to the public service boundary make this the strongest available routing candidate for the scheduler policy decision.
